title: Luminescent-based NAD+/NADH Detection in C. elegans, Mice, and Human Blood
author: Wang, Zhang, et al.
materials:
Timing: 20–30 min
20.Preparation of reconstituted luciferin detection reagent (RLDR) following the manufacturer’s instructions with modifications:a.Thaw the reconstitution buffer in the NAD/NADH-Glo Assay Kit.b.Equilibrate the reconstitution buffer and lyophilized luciferin detection reagent to 25°C.c.Transfer the entire content of the reconstitution buffer bottle to the amber bottle of lyophilized luciferin detection reagent.d.Mix by swirling or inversion to obtain a uniform solution.e.Aliquot reconstituted luciferin detection reagent into 15 mL centrifuge tubes, with 5 mL per tube.f.The solution can be stored at −20°C up to 3 months.
Note: Do not vortex or shake vigorously.
21.Preparation of reconstitute NAD cycling enzyme:a.Reconstitute one vial of NAD cycling enzyme by adding 275 μL of ddH2O.b.Mix by gently swirling the vial.c.Aliquot NAD cycling enzyme into 1.5 mL tubes, with 20 μL per tube.d.Store at −20°C for future usage. It can be freeze-thawed and reused up to twice.
Note: Store the Reductase Substrate at −80°C. Minimize multiple freeze-thaw cycles of all reagents by making several aliquots. All solution of reagents remains effective for a period of 3 month upon opening as indicated by the product manual.

steps.title: Prepare C. elegans samples
steps.instruction: Collect, wash, weigh, lyse, and deproteinize adult worms for NAD+/NADH detection.

substeps.instruction: Weigh an empty 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube (record as W1).
Add 1.5 mL M9 buffer to NGM plates, wash worms into the tube, let settle 1–2 min, and discard supernatant.

Resuspend worms in 1 mL M9 buffer, spin down, and repeat wash (steps b‑c) three times until supernatant is clear of bacteria (minimum 600 adult worms, e.g., ~250 worms per 10‑cm plate pooled from three plates).
Vacuum‑dry the tube with lid open for 10 min at 4 °C using a centrifugal vacuum concentrator.
Weigh the tube with worms (record as W2) and calculate worm mass (W2‑W1).
Add 400 µL ice‑cold 1× PBS to the tube.
Sonicate on a Diagenot Bioruptor Plus set to –8 °C: 10 cycles of 30 s ON / 30 s OFF at high power (keep tubes on ice throughout).
Transfer lysate to a pre‑cooled 10 kDa spin column (Cat.# MRCPRT010) and centrifuge 13 000 × g at 4 °C for 20 min.
Collect the flow‑through (effluent) and keep on ice for downstream NAD+/NADH detection.

steps.title: Prepare mouse muscle samples
steps.instruction: Harvest, weigh, freeze, homogenize, and deproteinize gastrocnemius muscle for NAD+/NADH detection.

substeps.instruction: Euthanize mouse according to approved protocol (CO₂ inhalation or cervical dislocation).
Spray mouse with 70 % ethanol, remove skin of left hind‑leg with sterile scissors/forceps, and expose gastrocnemius muscle, avoiding tendons.
Excise muscle, cut into small pieces, and place in a pre‑chilled sterile petri dish with PBS (keep tools on dry ice and work quickly).
Weigh an empty 1.5 mL tube (record as W1).
Wash dissected muscle twice with PBS.
Transfer tissue to the tube, weigh (record as W2), and compute tissue mass (W2‑W1).
If not processing immediately, snap‑freeze the tube in liquid nitrogen.
Transfer 50 mg of tissue to an ice‑cold lysis matrix D tube and add 400 µL ice‑cold 1× PBS.
Homogenize with FastPrep‑24 5G: speed = 6.0 m/s, adaptor = QuickPrep, 40 s, 3 cycles, 10 s pause between cycles.
Centrifuge the homogenate 13 000 × g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Transfer supernatant to a pre‑cooled 10 kDa spin column (Cat.# MRCPRT010) and centrifuge 13 000 × g at 4 °C for 30 min.
Keep the clarified effluent on ice for NAD+/NADH detection (repeat step if insufficient volume).

steps.title: Prepare mouse whole blood
steps.instruction: Collect, freeze, lyse, deproteinize, and dilute mouse blood for NAD+/NADH detection.

substeps.instruction: Remove food from cages 12 h before collection; keep water available.
Anesthetize mouse, confirm deep anesthesia (absence of reflexes), and decapitate.
Collect 100–200 µL blood from the carotid artery into a labeled EDTA tube.
Immediately snap‑freeze the tube in liquid nitrogen.
Transfer 100 µL blood to an ice‑cold lysis matrix D tube.
Homogenize using FastPrep‑24 5G (6.0 m/s, QuickPrep, 40 s, 3 cycles, 10 s pause).
Centrifuge 13 000 × g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Load supernatant onto a pre‑cooled 10 kDa spin column (Cat.# MRCPRT010) and centrifuge 13 000 × g at 4 °C for 30 min.
Dilute the eluate 1:3 with 1× PBS (add 150 µL PBS to 50 µL eluate; dilution factor = 4).
Keep the diluted sample on ice for NAD+/NADH detection.

steps.title: Prepare human whole blood
steps.instruction: Collect, store, lyse, deproteinize, and dilute human blood for NAD+/NADH detection.

substeps.instruction: Verify participant identity, obtain consent, and ensure fasting status.
Clean the median cubital vein, apply a tourniquet, and draw 5 mL blood into a labeled EDTA tube using a 30‑gauge needle (15°–30° angle).
Remove tourniquet, apply pressure, and secure site with gauze and tape; invert tube gently to mix.
If not processed immediately, store tube at –80 °C within 2 min.
Transfer 200 µL blood to an ice‑cold lysis matrix D tube.
Homogenize with FastPrep‑24 5G (6.0 m/s, QuickPrep, 40 s, 3 cycles, 10 s pause).
Centrifuge 13 000 × g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Load supernatant onto a pre‑cooled 10 kDa spin column (Cat.# MRCPRT010) and centrifuge 13 000 × g at 4 °C for 30 min.
Dilute eluate 1:3 with 1× PBS (add 150 µL PBS to 50 µL eluate).
If the blood is very viscous, first dilute 100 µL eluate with 100 µL PBS, then adjust final dilution to 1:1.5 by adding 150 µL PBS (final volume 250 µL).
Keep the diluted sample on ice for NAD+/NADH detection.

steps.title: Prepare assay reagents
steps.instruction: Reconstitute luciferin detection reagent and NAD‑cycling enzyme for the NAD/NADH‑Glo assay.

substeps.instruction: Thaw the reconstitution buffer from the NAD/NADH‑Glo kit and let it equilibrate to 25 °C.
Transfer the entire buffer to the amber bottle containing lyophilized luciferin detection reagent, mix by gentle swirling (no vortex).
Aliquot 5 mL of the reconstituted luciferin detection reagent into each 15 mL centrifuge tube; store at –20 °C (stable ≤3 months).
Add 275 µL ddH₂O to one vial of NAD‑cycling enzyme, swirl gently, and aliquot 20 µL into 1.5 mL tubes.
Store enzyme aliquots at –20 °C; they may be freeze‑thawed up to twice.
Note: keep Reductase Substrate at –80 °C and minimize freeze‑thaw cycles for all reagents.

steps.title: Isolate NAD+ and NADH
steps.instruction: Separate NAD+ from NADH in each sample using acid/base treatment and heat, then prepare plates for luminescence measurement.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 50 µL of each clarified effluent sample into a well of a white 96‑well luminometer plate.
Add 50 µL of base solution containing 1 % DTAB to the same well.
Shake the plate on a microplate shaker for 2 min.
Transfer 50 µL from this well into an empty adjacent well (leaving 50 µL behind).
To the original well (base‑treated), add 25 µL of 0.4 N HCl (acid‑treated sample).
Leave the transferred well untreated (remains base‑treated).
Seal the plate and incubate at 60 °C for 15 min.
Cool the plate at room temperature for 10 min.
Neutralize acid‑treated wells by adding 25 µL of 0.5 M Trizma base.
Neutralize base‑treated wells by adding 50 µL of HCl/Trizma base solution (as supplied with the kit).
Transfer 50 µL from each well into a new empty well to create duplicate measurements.

steps.title: Prepare NAD+/NADH standards
steps.instruction: Generate a series of NAD+ and NADH standards ranging from 0 to 400 nM for calibration.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 6 mL dilution buffer in a 15 mL tube by mixing 1.5 mL each of: PBS, base solution with 1 % DTAB, 0.4 N HCl, and 0.5 M Trizma base (1:1:1:1 ratio).
Dilute the 2 mM NAD+ stock and the 2 mM NADH stock separately with the dilution buffer to obtain 1 µM working solutions.
Create the following standard series (volumes of 1 µM stock + dilution buffer) to achieve final concentrations (nM) as listed:
• 0 nM: 0 µL stock + 200 µL buffer
• 10 nM: 2 µL stock + 198 µL buffer
• 20 nM: 4 µL stock + 196 µL buffer
• 40 nM: 8 µL stock + 192 µL buffer
• 60 nM: 12 µL stock + 188 µL buffer
• 80 nM: 16 µL stock + 184 µL buffer
• 100 nM: 20 µL stock + 180 µL buffer
• 120 nM: 24 µL stock + 176 µL buffer
• 140 nM: 28 µL stock + 172 µL buffer
• 160 nM: 32 µL stock + 168 µL buffer
• 180 nM: 36 µL stock + 164 µL buffer
• 200 nM: 40 µL stock + 160 µL buffer
• 240 nM: 48 µL stock + 152 µL buffer
• 280 nM: 56 µL stock + 144 µL buffer
• 320 nM: 64 µL stock + 136 µL buffer
• 360 nM: 72 µL stock + 128 µL buffer
• 400 nM: 80 µL stock + 120 µL buffer
Dispense 50 µL of each standard into designated wells of a 96‑well plate; replicate each concentration in separate wells.

steps.title: Analyze luminescence data
steps.instruction: Generate standard curves, calculate sample concentrations, and normalize to tissue weight or blood volume.

substeps.instruction: For each standard, compute the average luminescence of replicate wells.
Subtract the average blank (zero‑concentration) luminescence from all values to obtain net luminescence.
Plot net luminescence (y‑axis) versus known standard concentration (x‑axis) for NAD+ and separately for NADH using Excel or GraphPad Prism (v10.1.1).
Fit a smooth curve (linear regression) through each data set to obtain the standard‑curve equation.
Measure net luminescence of each sample well and interpolate its concentration from the appropriate standard curve.
Multiply the interpolated concentration by the sample‑specific dilution factor (e.g., ×4 for the 1:3 dilution of blood samples).
Normalize the corrected concentration:
– For C. elegans and mouse muscle: divide by the measured tissue weight (mg).
– For mouse or human blood: divide by the original sample volume (µL) used for lysis.
Report the final normalized NAD+ or NADH concentration for each biological sample.
